# WordPress standards (wp-dev-kit)

Security (escape, sanitize, nonces, `$wpdb->prepare`) lives in `wp-review.mdc`. This file covers the rest. If another rule in this repo is more specific (tokens, a11y, text domain), that rule wins.

## Coding standards
- Follow https://developer.wordpress.org/coding-standards/wordpress-coding-standards/. `phpcs` (config: `phpcs.xml.dist`) must report 0 errors on PHP files you touched. Pint owns formatting; WPCS owns security, i18n and WP API usage.
- In Claude Code, a hook runs phpcs after every PHP edit. Fix what it reports.
- Never add `phpcs:ignore` without a comment saying why.

## i18n
- Wrap every user-facing string in `__()`, `esc_html__()`, `esc_attr__()`, `_n()` or `_x()` with the text domain `walkridge`.

## theme.json
- Keep `"$schema": "https://schemas.wp.org/trunk/theme.json"` and `"version": 3`. Only use keys from https://developer.wordpress.org/block-editor/reference-guides/theme-json-reference/theme-json-living/. If unsure, check; don't invent settings.
- Use preset CSS vars (`var(--wp--preset--color--…)`), not hard-coded values. In Sage, never hand-edit the generated `public/build/assets/theme.json`.

## Accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA
Refs: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/quickref/ · https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/ · https://make.wordpress.org/themes/handbook/review/accessibility/
- Semantic HTML first: one `<h1>`, logical headings, landmarks, a working skip link.
- Everything works by keyboard alone. Focus is visible (2.4.7) and not hidden behind a sticky header (2.4.11).
- Contrast 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for UI and large text. Targets at least 24×24 CSS px (2.5.8). No drag-only actions (2.5.7).
- Visible text is part of the accessible name (2.5.3): don't put an `aria-label` on a link that already has visible text.
- Only name elements that can take a name: interactive elements, landmarks, or elements with a `role`. `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` on a plain `<span>` or `<div>` is ignored (axe `aria-prohibited-attr`); use visually hidden text or a real element instead.
- Form fields have labels, errors are announced, `autocomplete` is set where it applies. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Build menus, tabs, modals and accordions from ARIA APG patterns, not from memory.
- Never claim "this is accessible". Say what you tested (Lighthouse / axe / pa11y) and that a manual keyboard + VoiceOver pass is still needed.

## Before a PR
- Run `wp-review`, `phpcs`, `composer analyse` (PHPStan, if set up), `vendor/bin/pint --test` and `npm run build`, then ask the `wp-security-reviewer` subagent to review the diff.
- One tool writes, a different tool reviews (Bugbot / Claude GitHub Action / Codex). Matt approves anything that ships.
